title: House of Friendship food program funding moved
subtitle: Short special meeting also approved 2023 borrowing by-law and a closed session for education and training.
overview: Kitchener's first special Council meeting of 2023 was brief, lasting about four minutes of business. The main item was a funding agreement with House of Friendship, which had been deferred from the December 12 meeting.

Council moved funding of $158,621 for House of Friendship services out of the Tier 1 grant program and into the Neighbourhood Programs and services operating budget {{vote:m1}}. The General Manager of Community Services may sign a funding agreement every two years, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction. The money covers food programs at City facilities. For residents, this puts the food programs on a more stable, longer-term footing than an annual grant.

Council also passed a by-law authorizing borrowing for current expenditures in 2023, along with the by-law confirming the meeting's actions. Council then agreed to meet in closed session right after the meeting to receive education and training {{vote:m2}}. The minutes report no further detail on that session.

decisions.detail: Council moved $158,621 for House of Friendship services from the Tier 1 grant program into the Neighbourhood Programs and services operating budget {{vote:m1}}.
The General Manager, Community Services may sign a funding agreement with House of Friendship every two years, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction, to cover food programs at City facilities.

debate: The transcript records no discussion on the House of Friendship funding motion. The Mayor asked for discussion and the motion went straight to a vote.
The Mayor noted the item had been deferred from the December 12 meeting, but the transcript gives no reasons for the deferral or any arguments for or against.
